pages.name: Star phase voltage
pages.task: A 440 V star: what is each line's voltage to the star point?
pages.why: 440 ÷ 1.732 = 254 V. A star winding sees this, not 440 V.

pages.name: Both sides star
pages.text: With both sides in star, the hand sits at twelve: Yyn0. Each limb's windings share one flux. The clock fixes the HV line voltage A–B at twelve. The LV line voltage a–b is the hour hand, 30° an hour.

pages.name: Hour to degrees
pages.task: A name ends in 5. How far clockwise from twelve is its LV hand?
pages.why: 5 × 30 = 150°. Its LV line voltage sits 150° behind the HV's.

pages.name: Delta on the HV side
pages.text: With the HV in delta, the hand sits at eleven: Dyn11. Limb 1's HV winding carries A–B, at twelve. The LV winding a–n keeps time with it. The LV line voltage runs 30° ahead of a–n, so a–b sits one hour anticlockwise.
